static_traits.name: Zhou Ming
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with bandmates affected by self-doubt and self-criticism; has supportive bandmates and friends, but has not yet expressed the sense of failure and distress to them.
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness history; no previous psychotherapy or psychological problem history; has not experienced similar problems before.
static_traits.language_features: Clear and logical expression, good cooperation; able to self-reflect but strongly self-critical; tense mood, highly sensitive to mistakes.

basic_info.main_problem: At the most recent live performance, played wrong notes in a key passage; since then has persistently felt like a failure and believes they should quit the band.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to ease the sense of failure and self-doubt, recover passion for music, and improve overall physical and mental state.

special_situations.event: Made a wrong note during a key passage of a live performance, noticed by some audience members
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a mistake happens at a critical moment, it shows I do not deserve to be the band's guitarist and am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcing oneself to pursue perfection and practice doubly to avoid any errors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I messed up; I am just a failure; I should quit the band

special_situations.event: Every time thinking about the upcoming rehearsal or next performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make another mistake, everyone will be disappointed and it will prove I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Gaining a sense of control through continuous extra practice, trying to reduce errors to zero
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will mess up again; everyone will look down on me

special_situations.event: Considering whether to communicate one's feelings with bandmates and seek feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they point out my problems, it confirms I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding communication with others to avoid being evaluated or negated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I am no good / will look down on me

special_situations.event: After a performance, someone praised it and said the overall show was good
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as there is one mistake, all good performance does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replays mistakes, ignoring positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those praises do not count; my performance was poor

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and accepted as a 'qualified/excellent guitarist', and to maintain self-worth through stable performance
core_conflict.fear: Fear of disappointing others, of being negated and humiliated, worried one mistake will lead to exclusion
defense_goal: Avoiding being negated through pursuing perfection and self-criticism
Maintains avoidant communication to reduce harm from external evaluations

object_relations.object_representation: Picky others who may negate one (audience/bandmates)

object_relations.self_representation: A judged person prone to erring at critical moments
object_relations.object_representation: Judges who may ignore strengths and only see shortcomings

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor inquires whether I am willing to communicate with band partners and obtain real feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes others will confirm 'not good enough', attributing inner negation to others' thoughts (transference: projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a gentle, supportive tone, first empathize with the worries, then use open questions to guide distinguishing 'worries' from 'facts', inviting small steps to get real-world feedback.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reviewing the view that 'one mistake means overall failure'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating one mistake with total failure, understanding self and performance in all-good/all-bad terms (transference: splitting)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain a steady, non-judgmental tone, use clarification and contrast questions, help see strengths and shortcomings together, gradually introducing a more integrated view.

manifestations: After one mistake, equates self-worth and career meaning with a 'perfect performance'
Ignoring positive feedback and success fragments, falling into rumination on failure
outcomes: Decreased drive to practice, dreading rehearsals/performances, with withdrawal
Overall decline in sense of well-being

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy originally intended to be expressed outward or to seek support toward herself instead, restraining action impulses toward others or the environment.
manifestations: Have not expressed distress to supportive bandmates and friends
Turns the urge to communicate into self-criticism and extra practice
Choosing self-denial and bearing it alone when outside feedback is needed

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and excessive self-restriction and harshness, overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Excessively harsh and self-scrutinizing about one mistake
Excessively worrying about being negated when considering communicating with others
Constraining oneself with a 'must be perfect' standard

positive_force: Willing to try practicing and seeking counseling; has willingness to change
negative_force: Cognitive tendencies toward catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking
Excessively dependent on external evaluation and worried about disappointing others
Negating positive feedback, repeatedly ruminating on mistakes
Avoiding communication, causing relationship tension and blocking support

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophic self-labeling and thoughts of quitting the band
antecedent: After a mistake in a live performance
Thinking about the next rehearsal or performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralizing one mistake as total failure, defining self-worth by perfectionist standards, fearing negation and humiliation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potentially shameful and negating situations
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased motivation to practice, professional performance affected, overall happiness lowered

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids communicating feelings with bandmates and seeking feedback
antecedent: When asked whether they communicate with teammates
When considering expressing distress to teammates or seeking opinions
target_behavior.core_reason: Projecting inner worries of negation onto others, fearing confirmatory negation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome evaluations and emotional pain
target_behavior.consequence: Relationship tension, support unable to get in, staying stuck in self-doubt

target_behavior.behavior: Doubles practice when negative thoughts appear, pursuing perfection
antecedent: When thinking of mistakes or upcoming rehearsals/performances
When feeling strong self-doubt and failure
target_behavior.core_reason: Seeking a sense of control through extra practice, to undo the fear and uncertainty about mistakes
target_behavior.function: Gaining a controllable feeling and temporarily easing anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Increased stress and self-harshness, negative cognitions not yet improved, possibly further depleting motivation
